The four failed jobs were traced to obsolete description expectations, an obsolete closed-mock baseline entry, a legacy recovery fixture downgrading the whole database into the new credential-migration guard, and real elapsed time exceeding the authorization fixture’s one-second budget. The repair updates the contract assertions, shrinks the baseline, models the migrated NULL-draft row, and controls the auth fixture’s clock while retaining the unchanged deadline suite. Targeted types also caught a widened literal; upstream integration exposed a missing startup outbox-drain import. Both are repaired.

The integrated source tree passes **134 focused tests across 10 files**, affected agent/Gateway test type graphs, UI production types, scoped lint/formatting and the mock ratchet. Independent P0–P2 review of the CI repair found no actionable defects. Hosted CI is pending; this is not a claim that the new hosted run is green. The description explicitly keeps prior native captures qualified to their recorded revisions after the merge.

The existing ClawSweeper re-review is still active on the previous head, so no duplicate request has been submitted.

Evidence index for #177698. Current source is `7ecc42f61a92bc58d5a097edf20bcf2c46c66b2c`, incorporating named upstream `d5ada1406b917579c7591cda139923d0a78b893b`. The mixed frozen-cohort restore repair is now included. A retired leader no longer discards an owed sibling's FIFO reservation: the existing owner selects a surviving representative before and after requester lookup while retaining the whole frozen identity, owed timestamp, exact-member/generation checks and recovery-custody checks. Its two positive regressions fail on the pre-fix producer; whole-cohort retirement and generation replacement remain negative controls. The exact final regression also reproduces both failures on standalone #177661, whose updated branch is available for maintainer choice.

Current `7ecc42f61a9` resolves the next three actual conflicts: fallback factories preserve the same-profile/current-caller/client-cap tests, admission keeps early requester binding plus joined release with upstream rejection/context cleanup, and placement retains the exact-claim settler. 191 checks/eight files, core/two owning test-type graphs, typed lint/format and independent scoped P0–P2 review pass. The final derived annotation is type-only and was rechecked. Canonical private-QA runtime-profile build passes; current human passed; queued failed.

The named hosted failure in worker-turn-launcher is reproduced on the actual merged upstream source. Upstream moved plain local claims in-process, so clearing durable restart rows is no longer the current-claim retirement operation. The test uses the existing exact placement settler, retains the same reused run ID and distinct claim IDs, and still requires the old finally to leave the replacement untouched. No product logic changes for that CI repair.

At the earlier `c33ca7e8d7c` integration, **52 recovery/dispatch/mailbox/Stop tests and 75 placement-owner/sibling tests passed across seven files**. Core production and owning agent-session test types pass; the placement test graph, scoped lint/format, whitespace and both repairs' independent P0–P2 reviews pass. The mixed-cohort suite was rerun after the named upstream merge. Those counts remain revision-qualified. Broad exact-head CI remains the gate; current native execution is not inferred from these older counts.



Revision `70cca921f3f` changed only two comments and one test title after `c33ca7e8d7c`: it accurately labels explicit old-cohort removal as a scope-lifetime regression, rather than asserting that queue ACK naturally retires a product outbox. Runtime expressions, assertions and fixture execution are unchanged. The 127 focused checks and native handoff retain their actual `c33ca7e8d7c` source qualification. Formatting and whitespace pass for the wording edit.

The prior `918d0793534` integration resolves the actual reported conflict against upstream `6088df9dbf4f`. The manual helper-signature resolution preserves the complete outer contract and existing captured-current-caller, route and adapter guards. Native-child independent continuation remains selected exactly as upstream; the equivalent conditional option avoids an empty object spread, and the instance annotation derives from its existing canonical factory. The merged candidate passed 109 related owner checks and then seven targeted admission checks after option cleanup, core and owning agent-session test types, final typed lint/format and whitespace. Independent P0–P2 review with authority-owner context found no actionable defect; the last annotation-only cleanup changes no runtime expression. No declaration/line-limit exception was added. Previous native/compatibility captures retain their recorded heads.

### Authenticated queued policy effects at `139939f8165`

Three isolated runs at `139939f8165188c8ef740596980adaed67359c29` passed using real native 0.163.0, explicitly overriding the unchanged 0.162.1 manifest pin, and a scripted loopback provider. Distinct non-owner profiles authenticated through a configured trusted proxy; their initially unrestricted model policy and actual administrative role grant are disclosed.

| Case | Actual boundary and result |
| --- | --- |
| Positive | Real child completion bound the requester scope before queued ACK. After held predecessor cleanup released, the actual native continuation removed one disabled synthetic job, returned `{ok:true,removed:true}`, and finished normally with exact accepted run/session/selected-turn correlation. Complete canonical and all 18 SQL columns changed only by removing that job. |
| Profile-role reassignment | Canonical `users.setRole` acknowledged the actor's new reader role 62 ms after queued ACK; explicit cleanup-release intent followed at 63 ms. The exact queued run ended with `status: error`, `stopReason: rpc`, zero native input/removal frames and unchanged complete inventories. No normal release event occurred because the source unwound. |
| Model membership | Canonical `config.patch` changed the same role from unrestricted model membership to an empty allowlist, with unchanged profile/role/scopes, applied revision confirmed and no restart. Mutation ACK was 266 ms after queued ACK; explicit release intent was 294 ms, normal release 317 ms. The exact queued run reported the model-permission error below, with zero native input/removal frames and unchanged complete inventories. |

```json
{"status":"error","error":"Your operator role cannot use this model. Choose an allowed model or ask a gateway administrator to update your role's model policy."}
```

Each case joined its two actual native processes with exit zero/no signal, confirmed Gateway stop and proxy/provider cleanup, and removed task state. The aliased JSON projection retains actual safe receipt scalars plus explicitly derived chronology, counts and full-equality results; original mappings and raw captures remain private.

Earlier failed attempts remain unqualified: a pre-remap fixture model ceiling, then a correct finite-policy/unsupported-owned-route refusal. The passing model case is unrestricted→empty at the next queued model boundary; it does not prove initially finite policy enforcement on the loopback route or a cron commit-stage denial. Profile identity merging, scheduled execution, external inference and security-owner approval are not covered. The outbox retained its genuine dispatching custody and retired naturally after the positive final; no manual deletion or separate SQL absence snapshot is claimed.

A separate reviewer checked original source/authentication receipts, native wire and journals, canonical inventories, all 18 SQL columns and process cleanup. All 41 captured source owners were unchanged at conservative revision `9014549758f`; the later upstream integration changes start-owner/deadline handling, so that comparison does not extend to the whole current runtime.

### Conservative peer/human delivery at `9014549758f`

At source `9014549758f5dfc22da309ead4fda330992f645c`, three isolated scripted-provider/native cases qualified with clean teardown. The actual native runtime was0.163.0 through an explicit private QA override; the source dependency remains0.162.1.

- Default ordinary unrelated-peer `sessions_send` omitted `mode`. Its input was observable as queued while the original output item remained unfinished. The original native turn finished normally before a distinct native turn started. The queued run, actual tool reply, Gateway session incarnation, selected native turn and normal final matched; no marker-bearing native steer occurred.
- Explicit `mode:followup` produced the same separately admitted, correlated next-turn behavior.
- A genuine authenticated human `chat.send` received a native steer ACK for the original turn, appeared once in that turn’s raw provider input and native journal, and reached its normal final. Sampling occurred after response completion.

All three ended with exactly one canonical input row, zero pending inputs, no forced Stop, six actual native process exits with code0 and no signal, stopped Gateways/providers and removed task state.

This is conservative peer routing plus original-turn human consumption. It does not establish native collaboration mailbox timing parity, universal human mid-item preemption, late optional-result promotion, or authority after a child outbox retires. Peer runs may use a new physical native thread. No external inference, real-user conversation, deployment or owner approval is part of this evidence.

A second reviewer parsed original native ACKs/journals, canonical queued inputs, actual tool results, provider inputs, terminals and all cleanup receipts; no mismatch was found. Synthetic V2/non-lite model capability metadata is a disclosed QA override. Neither source authority nor runtime acceptance/accounting results were replaced.

Fixed the new `checks-ui-e2e (5/8)` failure in `8c962482a9b`.

Both sidebar-module recovery cases timed out clicking Retry while a synthetic reconnect was still pending. Upstream #177690 correctly disables Retry during an attempt; this older fixture had not settled that attempt. The fixture now uses the existing virtual-clock pattern, explicitly fails the pending mock socket, verifies Retry becomes enabled, and verifies that one manual retry creates exactly one replacement socket before normal reconnection.

Both viewport cases reproduced the same disabled-Retry failure locally before the repair. The complete module-boundary browser file now passes **15/15** cases in **69.96 seconds**, using existing system Chrome through the supported executable override. UI production types, lint/format, and independent P0–P2 review pass. Production code and timeout budgets are unchanged; hosted CI on this head is pending.

The relevant owners and original fixture are unchanged from pinned upstream; an exact-base CI reproduction was not run. The PR body retains the native evidence at its recorded revisions and documents that this commit changes only the UI test fixture.

### Recommended landing: Codex-like human steering now; preserve peer behavior pending a mailbox API

**The best peer solution is supported access to Codex’s existing native mailbox. Until that API exists, my recommendation is to preserve OpenClaw’s current peer scheduling and land the independent human steering repairs.** Broader peer steering is an optional maintainer decision, not a prerequisite for fixing humans.

Human input already has a supported native operation: `turn/steer`, bound to the exact active turn. Use that operation and let Codex choose its own interruption boundary; do not add a host-forced Stop/restart or an earlier interruption. Peer mail follows a different native path. A supported app-server mailbox operation would let OpenClaw match it without maintaining a Codex fork.

The distinction is measured, not hypothetical. At `7daf590c302a`, actual isolated Gateway/native traces observed native child-to-parent peer mail consumed after commentary item completion but before response completion. Authenticated human input and real host `sessions_send(mode="steer")` input were both consumed after response completion in the measured WebSocket branch. Host peer steering therefore failed the native-mailbox parity comparison cleanly. This does not establish timing for all phases, tools, transports or adapters. All state/content was synthetic, the provider was scripted/local, native 0.163.0 explicitly overrode the unchanged 0.162.1 manifest pin, and all seven native processes exited cleanly. Earlier failed collectors retain their qualifications.

The [native mailbox loop](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/83086188ae0614bd882818ff1aa23f3194962012/codex-rs/core/src/session/turn.rs#L2869-L2937) and [user-steer protocol](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/83086188ae0614bd882818ff1aa23f3194962012/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/turn.rs#L311-L340) explain why using the same host route for peers does not reproduce native peer behavior. Delayed output events cannot supply the missing atomic mailbox operation.

Until a supported API is available, preserve delayed/separate-turn peers and the narrowly approved exceptions, including [#160842](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160842) and its [explicit owner acceptance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160842#issuecomment-5882083686). Maintainers may instead approve the existing human-steer approximation for peers, acknowledging the timing compromise. That is not my recommended default.

**Implemented at `9014549758f`:** ordinary peer sends, explicit `followup` and returned results retain separate admission and correlated completion. Default self-sends stay separate; explicit `steer` and the existing zero-wait own-child/run-scoped exceptions retain their access checks. The broader returned-result live-steer branch is removed, and delivery tests, tool guidance and docs agree. The new regressions fail on the broader-routing parent; all 143 affected tests and the canonical production/test type checks pass. Isolated native runtime validation is being completed separately; no blanket timing-parity claim is made. Accepted human reply-obligation promotion remains a separate product decision. Security-owner acceptance is also still required; neither can be inferred from Codex behavior or passing tests.

### Calibrated proposal: repair human steering; let maintainers choose peer policy

I am revising my earlier recommendation to generalize active delivery for all compatible busy input. Human steering and peer-mail timing are different contracts. Improving human steering should not require maintainers to accept peer messages arriving through the human-input path.

**The conservative landing choice is to preserve existing peer scheduling, including its already approved narrow steering exceptions, while accepting the independent human steering and lifecycle repairs.** Maintainers can instead choose broader peer steering through the existing API, with its timing compromise documented. Neither choice should be presented as forced by Codex behavior or necessary for the human fixes.

The source candidate currently still contains the broader busy-peer/followup proposal. This is a review decision, not a claim that the candidate already preserves the old peer default. The selected behavior must be implemented and its regressions reconciled before merge.

The distinction is supported by actual isolated traces at `7daf590c302a`: a genuine native collaboration child-to-parent message was consumed after commentary item completion and before response completion. Authenticated human input and a real host `sessions_send(mode="steer")` were both consumed after response completion on the measured WebSocket branch. All retained the original recipient thread/turn, one attributed input echo and normal finals; all seven native processes exited cleanly. The host-peer trace is a clean failing parity observation, not a parity pass. All data/state was synthetic and the provider scripted/loopback. Native 0.163.0 explicitly overrode the unchanged 0.162.1 manifest pin. Pending tools, other phases and other transports remain uncovered; earlier collector failures retain their qualifications.

That evidence does not justify forcing a peer policy change. Using `turn/steer` for peers can avoid waiting for an entire OpenClaw turn, but inherits human-input timing, which can differ from the native peer mailbox in either direction. Retaining delayed peer delivery has a coordination-latency cost but avoids adopting that approximation without approval. Native acknowledgment, transcript recording and model consumption must remain distinct under either choice.

The preferred eventual integration is a supported app-server operation exposing Codex's existing peer mailbox. Its [native item-boundary handling](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/83086188ae0614bd882818ff1aa23f3194962012/codex-rs/core/src/session/turn.rs#L2869-L2937) is distinct from the [user-steer protocol](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/83086188ae0614bd882818ff1aa23f3194962012/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/turn.rs#L311-L340). Maintainers can pursue that upstream API without this PR making a native fork a prerequisite. Host event timing and forced Stop/restart are not substitutes.

[#160842](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160842) remains a deliberate, narrowly approved repair, not a mistake: Peter [accepted zero-wait parent-to-busy-child steering](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160842#issuecomment-5882083686), preserving waited sends, ordinary peer targets and explicit followup. The new choice is whether to extend those semantics. The shared controller's exact execution owner, independent source authorization, reply accounting and explicit delivery outcomes remain useful without that extension.

The built-in cooperative-wait repair at `980116042b1` lets already admitted human/peer input wake `subagents wait` without cancelling children. Its 46 affected tests and checks pass, but it neither changes which peers are admitted nor supplies native mailbox parity. It is not deployed. Product decisions and security-owner acceptance remain separate; this comment infers neither from Codex nor from passing tests.

### Proposed decision: adopt Codex-style delivery to active work

I recommend accepting the proposed busy-followup behavior, rather than restoring separate-turn scheduling as the default for compatible input. OpenClaw's [stated priorities](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/782e8d2f836419978ef11684f98802b8a837d47e/VISION.md#L24-L39) include reliable sessions, subagents and better agent harnesses. The user experience should meet or exceed Codex's responsiveness: an update relevant to ongoing work should reach that work while it can still influence the result.

This is a concrete source comparison. In Codex, [`followup_task` selects `TriggerTurn`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/a956835d020762cb2b570053af06f643a11c0ecc/codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/multi_agents_v2/followup_task.rs#L42-L49), whose [contract](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/a956835d020762cb2b570053af06f643a11c0ecc/codex-rs/core/src/agent/types.rs#L56-L62) is delivery to an active turn or starting work when idle. Its [tool definition](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/a956835d020762cb2b570053af06f643a11c0ecc/codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/multi_agents_spec.rs#L217-L244) specifies delivery at message boundaries while sampling or after the pending tool call. `send_message` shares the submission owner and differs in whether it wakes an idle recipient. Neither name inherently requires waiting for a busy recipient's entire turn to finish.

That distinction matters operationally. For example, a dependency-ready update should reach work waiting on that dependency, rather than wait behind its completion. On long-running tasks, mandatory separate-turn scheduling can delay that update for tens of minutes or hours. Requiring the operator to interrupt the recipient manually defeats agent coordination. Delaying an update until the computation it changes has finished is a poor default, and can strand work waiting for that update. A historical escape hatch is a compatibility consideration, not by itself a reason to preserve that user experience.

The proposal retains one captured execution and its permissions. Compatible busy input joins it; idle recipients start normally. This change adds no explicit `turn/interrupt` operation, but that alone does **not** establish equal preemption timing. Further source inspection found that host peer messages currently use Codex user steering; native peer messages use a separate mailbox and completed-output boundary. The configured transport matters: three independently audited isolated traces at `7daf590c302a` now show native child-to-parent mail consumed after commentary completes and before response completion, while both authenticated human input and host `sessions_send(mode="steer")` wait until response completion on the measured WebSocket branch. That is a clean host-peer contract mismatch with extra waiting, not proof of equal timing or a passing parity test. Other transport branches can behave differently. Exact original-turn consumption, attributed echoes, normal finals and all seven native process exits were verified; all data was synthetic and the provider local/scripted. Native 0.163.0 was an explicit override of the unchanged 0.162.1 manifest pin. Pending tools and other phases/transports remain uncovered. The built-in cooperative-wait fix at `980116042b1` now lets admitted human/peer input wake `subagents wait` without cancelling children; its paired regressions and affected checks pass. It does not implement the missing native host-peer mailbox API. Matching human and peer behavior independently across runtime adapters remains an explicit unfinished requirement. Codex also [defers late peer mail after the answer boundary](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/a956835d020762cb2b570053af06f643a11c0ecc/codex-rs/core/src/session/tests.rs#L12432-L12467), so this is not a claim that all input is consumed instantly. Admission is distinct from consumption and from a separately correlated final response.

Accepted-human reply accounting is a related OpenClaw-specific choice: once the backend accepts a person's question, the optional/silent policy of the original background work should not erase the obligation to answer it. That obligation changes only after proven acceptance; it does not grant new tools or execution authority.

[#160842](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160842) already adopted this principle for one important case: a parent's default zero-wait message to its own busy child. It moved the steering decision ahead of separate-turn completion custody and acknowledged admission without waiting for transcript consumption. Peter [explicitly accepted that change](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160842#issuecomment-5882083686), while preserving waited sends, ordinary peer targets and explicit `followup`. That was a deliberate narrow fix, not an error this proposal needs to discredit. This PR generalizes the accepted steering principle through the shared controller and explicitly proposes revising the remaining busy-followup contract. It keeps the admission-versus-consumption distinction and the receiver's execution owner. We should evaluate that extension against Codex-style responsiveness and the actual authority proofs, rather than treat the old eligibility limits as the desired user experience. Maintainer approval remains required, as does the separate security-owner review; neither is being inferred from Codex or from passing tests. Fresh queued allowed-effect, exact-run cancellation, original-source revocation and stable-to-candidate compatibility cases now pass with the qualifications recorded in the PR body. Profile/model-policy controls and human/peer output-boundary parity remain open. Existing failed-collector and containment qualifications are preserved.

### Current-head queued authority after exceptional outbox retirement

At `e44f11ece93e98d89ca46d03e3dee67052e82ac0`, two isolated Gateway/real Codex app-server traces now exercise the previously unproved **exceptional** queued-authority lifetime.

A real authenticated owner creates a disabled synthetic automation, starts a managed child and yields. The continuation binds its scope before the queued ACK, waits for predecessor cleanup, and starts normally. While its native provider response is held before the automation call, the collector injects one neutral exception into observation of the outer `withSubagentProgressDraft` delivery promise. The original promise, callbacks, signals, arguments, inner recovery classifier and execution remain live and are independently joined. The unchanged requester-wake catch classifies the exception and performs canonical retirement. Both the raw SQLite read and canonical decoder confirm the **whole exact old child row is absent before the native automation call**. No row is manually deleted, and no authority, delivery result or guard is replaced.

- **Allowed:** the same accepted run/session/native turn removes only the selected disabled job, returns the actual successful native tool receipt and completes with a correlated normal native final/Gateway terminal. Complete canonical inventory and every stored column verify exactly two jobs becoming one, with the surviving record unchanged. No outbox replay occurs.
- **Revoked:** after the same retirement, the actual native remove reaches the real `cron.get` return gate. A separately authenticated keeper canonically revokes the original device before the unchanged post-await checks resume. The exact accepted run receives RPC cancellation, its actual native tool receipt is aborted/unsuccessful, and both jobs remain identical across all 18 stored columns. Native input was already consumed, and cancellation was recorded before effect-gate release: this proves cancellation with no storage effect, **not isolated attribution to the final cron commit guard**.

Both traces pass root and independent raw-receipt/source-pin audits. All four observed native processes exit zero with null exit signals; Gateway, provider, task state and launcher bootstrap are joined/cleaned. No live Gateway or business data is changed.

**Scope and retained failures:** this is a disclosed outer-observer fault injection, not a natural public-RPC or benign early-cleanup reproduction. The actual prepared policy is `current-request`; these captures do not prove the distinct `completion-handoff` policy after retirement, profile reassignment, model-policy membership changes or scheduled execution. Official native **0.163.0** is an explicit, verified task-only override of source manifest **0.162.1**; inference is scripted locally and all data is synthetic.

The earlier inner-observer experiment remains **failed as early-retirement proof**: the existing recovery classifier preserved its pending outbox instead. Its cleanup released the held provider and performed the selected synthetic removal; it is neither effect-free nor normal-final proof. It must not be conflated with these passing outer-boundary cases. An unused late-race denial flag in the positive collector is not an actual denial and is excluded from the claims; the real gate, native result, terminal and full inventories determine the outcome.

Security-owner acceptance of authority lifetimes/comparison identity and the maintainer decision on accepted-human optional reply promotion remain required. These traces are evidence, not owner approval or a claim that hosted CI is green.

@clawsweeper re-review

Please perform a fresh review using the revised title and PR body, rather than treating the earlier steering-only summary as the proposal. This request is intentionally separate from the review started before that rewrite. Head remains `48e86662660ee3b8270fb1c4fe2309cb3bcbcb8b`; the code has not changed with this editorial correction.

nodes.body: ## Actual completion-handoff continuation: native boundary proof Tested **c3efd0744574c6920dda4af1066b6d6058053a54** with the source-declared official Codex **0.162.1**, with no native-version, catalog or feature override. These are new executions of this head, rather than reuse of the earlier current-request captures. Both cases use an isolated real Gateway, three independently paired devices belonging to the same authenticated synthetic owner, actual managed `sessions_spawn`/`sessions_yield`, a retained canonical child envelope and the real one-use settle-batch handoff. The actual tool-policy owner selects **`completion-handoff`** before human input is sent. Native app-server requests/results are forwarded unchanged; only model inference is scripted locally. Hash-pinned instrumentation records original owner results. A scheduling hold after actual requester-yield settlement keeps the original result observable until the completion is accepted; it does not replace the settlement result. Human preparation separately pauses after its original await and before its unchanged guard. It supplies no authority, acceptance, backend result or replacement native input. | Case | Observed result | | --- | --- | | Authorized human | One actual `turn/steer` against the captured completion thread/turn, one matching native ACK, one selected raw provider input, one native user echo, one saved human input and final. That same completion turn finishes normally; no foreign-marker input. | | Incoming source revoked during preparation | The keeper revokes only the incoming device's operator token after original preparation has awaited and before its guard resumes. The original guard reports `operator source authority is no longer active`. Zero marker submissions anywhere on the native wire, provider transport or native journals; zero committed human transcript inputs/finals. The original completion owner stays valid and its completion finishes normally. | Selected original receipt values and independently derived counts follow; identifiers and marker content are aliased. This is not a verbatim complete wire dump. ```json { "positive": { "consumedHandoff": {"kind":"subagent-completion","settleBatch":true,"childEnvelopeVerified":true}, "actualPolicy": {"requesterPolicySource":"completion-handoff"}, "nativeRequest": {"method":"turn/steer","params":{"threadId":"completion-thread","expectedTurnId":"completion-turn","input":[{"type":"text","text":"synthetic-human-input"}]}}, "nativeResult": {"turnId":"completion-turn"}, "selectedRawProviderInputs":1, "nativeUserEchoes":1, "savedHumanInputs":1, "savedHumanFinals":1, "completionTerminal":{"status":"ok","turnId":"completion-turn"} }, "revokedSource": { "orderedBoundary":["original preparation awaited","incoming device B operator token revoked by keeper C","original guard resumed","source authority rejected"], "actualError":"operator source authority is no longer active", "nativeMarkerSubmissions":0, "rawProviderMarkerInputs":0, "nativeJournalMarkerInputs":0, "committedHumanTranscriptInputs":0, "cancelledAdmissionReceipts":1, "queuedInputsAtFinalReadback":0, "completionOwner":"A (still valid)", "completionTerminal":{"status":"ok","turnId":"completion-turn"} } } ``` The revoked sender's early `chat.send` started ACK is followed by an aborted terminal and a **retained cancelled admission receipt**, with queuedCount zero. This is rejection before native submission, not zero canonical bookkeeping or proof of a subsequent restart/replay. Each case preserves the complete preexisting one-row automation inventory, including all 18 raw stored columns. Independent raw audits compare source/build/fixture/native hashes, original handoff/envelope/policy observations, wire/provider/journal/history correlations and cleanup. All four owned native processes across the two cases exit **0 with no terminating signal**; ordinary teardown SIGTERMs are recorded, with no forced fallback. Gateway, provider, isolated state and bootstrap cleanup complete. The initial yielding parent is interrupted during supported handoff cleanup; the completion owns a **new** native thread and finishes normally. This is not initial-parent physical-thread continuity. **Scope:** synthetic data only, scripted inference, ordinary full-policy same-profile owners. This closes the distinct real-native completion-handoff positive and revoked-source rejection gap; it does not add proof of native peer-mailbox behavior, optional-reply promotion, profile/model-policy changes, early outbox retirement or an isolated automation commit guard. Earlier failed collectors, containment/SIGKILL qualifications and revision-specific limits remain intact. Security-owner acceptance and the remaining maintainer decisions still require their owners. ## Off-roster title/duration: inspected browser comparison These are **isolated producer-to-renderer browser captures**, not a claimed reproduction of the failed CI run's full-app ordering. A real session capability observes the current descriptor and processes a bounded 200-row synthetic list that omits that session. The real title/metadata producers receive an explicitly absent selected-row argument; their actual outputs feed the real Solid header and transcript, using normal transcript commit/measurement and product CSS. No pane roster is assigned to manufacture a race; no producer result or layout measurement is replaced, and no displayed text is edited. The same frozen fixture runs on c3 and a counterfactual browser composition compiled from c3 with **only the two repaired UI owners reverted to their pre-repair e44 versions**. The latter fails the exact-title assertion after recording `New session` / `Worked`; c3 passes exact title, `Worked for 3 minutes`, absent permission-bearing selection and read-only metadata assertions. Both captures use 1200×900 Chromium and actual visible element bounds. The screenshots are unedited, synthetic-only, and inspected. Full-app local baseline replays passed, so they remain **non-reproductions**, not failing-before evidence. Earlier setup failures (missing observation, unissued list read, projection reinsertion, screenshot destination/locator and incomplete fixture layout/commit) are retained separately; none is credited as a product failure. Existing Solid diagnostic warnings are also retained. This controlled component comparison proves the producer/rendered-state repair; it does not establish the historical CI interleaving. **Before/after images are now attached and verified.** Both hosted PNGs are byte-identical to the inspected synthetic originals. **Before — only the two UI owners reverted:** `New session` / `Worked`. **After — repaired producers:** `Synthetic observed conversation` / `Worked for 3 minutes`. Update after upstream conflict integration: current head is `0f78424994631408fbeed838bb7df25991d7ba40` over `5a0b5006d5fcb72f238c3c587395bf38591971ad`. The sole conflict adopts upstream [#178510](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178510)'s title implementation verbatim, preserving the separate read-only metadata repair. The same browser composition passes after integration and produces the identical inspected after-image; 76 affected UI tests, core/UI production types and scoped lint/format pass. All 34 source pins of these native captures match the integrated tree, but **the native executions above remain c3 executions**, not a fresh run of the merged binary. The same inspected images are now embedded above and verified against their original bytes. Security-owner acceptance, maintainer decisions and hosted CI remain separate gates.

## Remaining Muse proof: actual Gateway stream and persisted final

This supplies the bounded Gateway trace requested in [revision 7](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177698#issuecomment-6276848335), executed on **`0f78424994631408fbeed838bb7df25991d7ba40`** using a fresh build of that exact head.

**Boundary exercised:** authenticated `chat.send` and `sessions.messages.subscribe` → the registered production Muse harness → unmodified official `@muse-code/sdk` **1.4.4** → a subprocess serving scripted synthetic MSP frames → the normal Gateway assistant stream and canonical transcript writer. The external-process fixture is adapted from the existing offline lane at `scripts/e2e/lib/muse-runtime/` and `extensions/muse/src/test-support/fake-muse.mjs`. No SDK/Turn mock, replacement harness result, authority override, or transcript-writer substitute is used.

The external fixture sends `item/delta("started:")` **before** the actual `turn/start` ACK. The SDK awaits that ACK before returning the Turn to the harness; its delta iterator is live-only while `items()` replays the fold. This forces the same late-attachment condition as the regression. The collector then **requires the Gateway client to receive `started:` before it releases the suffix**. A terminal-only correction cannot satisfy this check.

The following is a field-whitelisted excerpt of the actual raw receipts. Times are milliseconds relative to the native prefix. Run, session, turn, and item identifiers are consistently replaced with synthetic aliases; native and Gateway sequences are separate domains.

```jsonl
{"at":0,"owner":"MSP","seq":10,"event":"item/delta","item":"message-1","delta":"started:"}
{"at":1,"owner":"MSP","seq":12,"event":"turn/start ACK","status":"accepted","nativeTurn":"turn-1"}
{"at":21,"owner":"Gateway client","seq":6,"event":"agent/assistant","item":"message-1","delta":"started:","snapshot":"started:"}
{"at":47,"owner":"MSP","seq":15,"event":"item/delta","item":"message-1","delta":" hello"}
{"at":47,"owner":"MSP","seq":16,"event":"item/completed","item":"message-1","text":"started: hello"}
{"at":47,"owner":"MSP","seq":18,"event":"turn/completed","terminal":"completed"}
{"at":95,"owner":"Gateway client","seq":7,"event":"agent/assistant","item":"message-1","delta":" hello"}
```

Results:

- Gateway wire deltas: **`["started:", " hello"]`**. Their derived cumulative values are `started:` then `started: hello`; the second wire event intentionally omits the cumulative `text` field under `projectAssistantWireDelta`.
- Prefix, ACK, and suffix correlate to the same actual native process/session/turn; both Gateway text events correlate to that exact native item and the submitted run, in increasing sequence, with no assistant replacement frame.
- `agent.wait` returned **`status: "ok"`**. The terminal lifecycle reports **`aborted: false`**, visible final `started: hello`, and settled execution. No `turn/interrupt` was submitted.
- The authenticated client’s `chat.history` and a separate canonical Gateway history read both return **one assistant message, exactly `started: hello`**. Streaming equality is a separate required check; neither final readback can substitute for it.
- A subsequent empty `chat` replacement/reset frame is retained in the raw capture. The no-replacement assertion concerns the `agent/assistant` stream, which delivered both complete live chunks before that frame.
- Canonical QA lifetime cleanup reports **`process: "confirmed-stopped", errors: []`**. Both external process exit receipts are **0**, both PIDs are absent, and temporary runtime state is removed. The fixture has an explicitly disclosed SIGTERM-to-normal-exit handler; this run’s exit receipts have no shutdown-signal event and the official SDK teardown was unchanged.

**Qualifications retained:** this is an actual local Gateway/production Muse harness/real SDK trace with a scripted external MSP server, **not** a signed-in official Muse CLI or real Meta inference run. All input/output is synthetic, execution is read-only, and no production service, credential, configuration, or data was used or changed. Isolated HOME/state/config/XDG values were established before imports; inherited credentials and proxy settings were excluded. The collector and 37 SDK/Muse/build inputs were frozen before execution. Fixture SHA-256: `0de80406539a779096a88723da014db0bee9d673adebf82eb4f3c78845638063`.

An independent raw-receipt audit passed **91 checks**, including all 37 frozen file pins. Its initial overstrict comparison of entire history response objects is preserved; only the volatile `snapshotAt` changed by 6 ms between readbacks, while messages and all other fields match. The raw logs also retain an isolated QA-bootstrap WAL checkpoint-busy warning; it is unclassified and did not produce a cleanup error.

The first capture is preserved as a **failed collector assertion**, not a passing run: the product delivered the correct two chunks and saved final, but the collector incorrectly required cumulative `text` on the second wire delta. After checking the Gateway wire owner, only that assertion was corrected; exact delta equality, required pre-suffix prefix, no replacement, and final persistence checks remain. No product source changed and no timeout/retry or product failure expectation was relaxed. The complete corrected capture is the passing run reported above. The earlier SDK red/green tests remain supporting evidence, separate from this Gateway capture.

This closes the supplied-evidence gap for the Muse prefix repair. It does **not** grant the security/session-owner decisions about authority lifetimes or optional-human reply promotion, and does not replace or broaden any earlier revision-qualified authority/UI proof.

Independent raw audit: 91 checks. The trace explicitly qualifies the scripted external MSP boundary and preserves failed collector/audit attempts, the later chat reset and bootstrap warning; it does not claim official Muse CLI/Meta inference. No product code changed for this proof.

<!-- consolidation-ci-e530-186be068-v1 -->
## CI diagnosis and upstream conflict repair

The six red indicators reported on `0f78424994631408fbeed838bb7df25991d7ba40` were three failed test jobs, `openclaw/ci-gate` reported both as a failed check run and a failed commit status, and one failed `openclaw/security-sensitive-review` status. The two failed commit statuses both described missing maintainer approval; they are not two independent security/session-owner checks. The test failures completed around 17:20–17:21 UTC; the new Muse proof was published at 17:43 UTC. That proof-only update introduced no code revision and did not cause these already-recorded failures.

| Failed test job | Observed failure | Diagnosis / action |
|---|---|---|
| [Node changed compact large 23](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39461306759/job/118764703533) | Embedded-maintenance budget case expected one flush, observed none | Full owning file passes 21/21 locally under Bun. Determining test/producer/budget/maintenance sources match the actual CI base. Original Linux CI cause remains **unknown**. |
| [Node compact small 5](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39461306759/job/118764703213) | Session Share source-replacement case received a physical-owner validation error | Full owning integration file passes 12/12 locally under Bun. Seventeen determining source/test files match the actual CI base. Original Linux CI cause remains **unknown**. |
| [UI E2E 1/8](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39461306759/job/118764700842) | Native touch gesture produced no drag | Adopted upstream [#178578](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178578), which routes the gesture through Chromium's touch emulator. Existing distance, inertia, direction and reader-preservation assertions remain. |

These are exact-job observations for GitHub's test merge `b546c1f478924ea673ea5254c3de3ead7b035bf7` (PR head `0f784…` integrated with base `4c7a1654f8f4a1dd2ecab4c421419f1093bc2d65`). Passing macOS replays and source equality do **not** establish an inherited failure, a flake, or a production fix. The base workflow was green but skipped the relevant heavy test lanes, so it supplies no executed-base comparison for these failures. Both backend failures remain recorded without a speculative patch or weaker guard/assertion.

Integration `186be068940b0a2b2c1311666a96bc86ff2fa958` merges upstream `e5302ee39c532afe0e2874990867b06f1e523bf5` to resolve the reported conflict and include the existing touch repair. The sole manual conflict retains this PR's exact-session, allowlisted transcript metadata projection; it accepts upstream's other cold-title/hydration changes and all new tests. A whole observed descriptor is not substituted into selected-session control props. Independent applied-resolution review found no P0–P2 issue.

Validation on the resolved integration tree: **91 UI tests pass**. The committed `186be…` build then passes **4 Chromium browser cases against the mocked Gateway** (mobile widget scrolling and all three cold-load anchors), **21 maintenance tests under Bun**, and **12 Session Share integration tests under Bun**. Core/UI production types, scoped typed lint/format, whitespace, and the canonical runtime/private-QA build pass. All owned runners joined. The build retains the startup-JS gzip advisory; no budget was changed. These local results are macOS evidence; they do not turn the original Linux failures into an established fix.

The earlier native completion-handoff execution remains qualified to c3; all 34 pinned production/test owners still match. The Muse Gateway capture remains an execution of `0f784…`; its 12 direct Muse production/test source pins are unchanged. These source comparisons permit scoped reuse and do not claim new native/Muse executions on `186be…`. Prior exceptional-capture, UI-image, authority-lifetime and reply-policy qualifications remain intact.

Hosted CI on the new head and explicit security/session-owner acceptance remain separate landing gates. No production Gateway or business session was changed.

### Recovery-compaction follow-up at `24bb99cfcf9`

A human message arriving during recovery compaction could be permanently downgraded to a followup: the same logical operation survived, but its detached backend left an already-resolved readiness promise behind. New input now waits for that exact operation’s next backend. Previously captured attachments remain fenced; Stop, cancellation, finalization, yield, and owner replacement still release or reject waiting input.

Recovery also now publishes its own compaction lifecycle, independently of optional hook text. Hidden runs deliver start/end through the existing authorized session subscription. Hook notices do not duplicate lifecycle/accounting or clear the UI status timer, and optional lifecycle-progress callbacks cannot block compaction.

Validation:
- The old producer fails the human-admission regression. The old Gateway transport fails all three positive compaction-delivery assertions; the three exclusion controls pass. Empty-notice recovery and UI notice-timer regressions also fail before their fixes.
- 174 focused tests pass across the affected owner/sibling suites. The affected controller/steering suites were rerun after the final lifecycle cleanup; 50 Gateway tests passed after extracting event selection into its existing admission module. Core/UI production types, typed lint, formatting, commit hooks, and the runtime/private-QA build pass. The existing startup-JS size advisory remains.
- A real isolated Gateway running the built-in OpenClaw runtime received a scripted HTTP context-overflow response and held its actual summary request. A human message was submitted once while compaction was held. After release, one human-bearing provider request and the human’s reply occurred on the original execution; the canonical human row appeared once and the server pending-input queue was empty. Compaction start preceded release and successful end followed it; compaction was accounted once. The observer, Gateway, provider, proxy, and bus joined normally, with Gateway exit code zero and no forced containment.

All proof inputs and message content were synthetic. This is an actual Gateway/controller/compaction flow with a scripted external Responses provider, not real-model inference or a reproduction of the private live session. Raw captures remain private. The first collector attempt failed its temporary-path canonicalization guard before Gateway startup; it is preserved as setup-only evidence. Earlier native/Muse captures retain their recorded revisions and scenario scope; this change does not claim a fresh native-runtime capture or resolve maintainer/security-owner decisions.

This revision has not been deployed to the operator Gateway.

nodes.body:
@enki I pushed two commits to this branch (fast-forward on top of `26d5d608da7`):

**`d18b29691a6` fix(agents): keep owed yielded cohort wakes and best-effort compaction notices**

1. **Owed yielded cohort wakes.** Restore (`subagent-announce-controller-source.ts`) and main-session recovery (`main-session-restart-recovery-target.ts`) treated a retired child as a retired requester wake. On main, `retireSubagentObligationsInContext` keeps a retired member's wake in a yielded cohort when the requester hasn't been told, so its one continuation reports the cancellation, and live dispatch reserves the mailbox for it (`reserveSubagentControllerSource(settledBatch[0]…)`, gated only by `isRequesterSettleDeliveryClosed`). After a restart:
   - restore reserved nothing, so newer human input went ahead of the owed notice;
   - recovery marked the main session (`marked: 1`) while the wake was still owed, so the session could be resumed by both recovery and the wake.

   Restore now picks the wake owner the way live dispatch does (first live member, or the first member of a yielded cohort). Recovery uses `expectsCompletionMessage` again for the recovery purpose. Ordinary waves still reserve nothing once every member retires.

   **This reverses two expectations of yours.** The mailbox `killed` / `suppressed` / `retired during lookup` cases now reserve for yielded cohorts, and I added non-yielded variants that keep your "no reservation" expectation. `whole batch retires during lookup` now reserves. In the recovery-yield suite, `killed dispatching` expects `marked: 0`, and I removed `rejects a yielded handoff if its live child obligation is killed before commit` because killing the child no longer changes the continuation. All 5 new or flipped cases fail on the previous head for exactly this reason.
2. **Compaction hook notices are now best-effort.** They awaited the serialized agent-event queue, so a held optional `start` progress callback blocked recovery compaction until the safety timeout (reproduced: 120s timeout). They now use `runBestEffortCallback` like start/end, so order is kept but compaction never waits on them. Covered by a `hook notices` case in the existing "does not wait for an optional progress callback" test.
3. I also dropped three exports in `reply-tool-authority-inbound.ts` that had no callers and failed the dead-export scan.

Production net −3 lines, tests net −32. Focused suites pass: 486 tests across mailbox, recovery, `subagents/announce`, compaction runtime and reply compaction. Core, extensions and UI typecheck clean. One failure remains and is pre-existing: `subagent-announce.requester-settle-pause.test.ts` reads a stale `/tmp/openclaw-agent.sqlite`. It fails identically without these commits; that's a test-isolation leak I'll file separately.

**`6f5fca7d891` chore: move unrelated fixes out of the session consolidation**

These were independent of the SessionController lifecycle, so they now live in their own PRs, unchanged and with you as author:

- #178837 Muse streamed-prefix fix (your Gateway stream proof is linked there)
- #178839 off-page chat title / run metadata
- #178840 xAI device-code test cleanup
- #178841 UI reconnect-retry e2e settle

The "Muse Gateway stream proof" evidence in this PR's body now belongs to #178837.

Note: this push invalidates the security-sensitive approval for the previous head, so it needs a fresh `/allow-security-sensitive-change` on `6f5fca7d891`.

@enki I stacked real-Gateway e2e coverage for this PR in #178985 (base branch `stack/pr-177698` mirrors this head, `6f5fca7d891`). It drives `chat.send`, Stop, `sessions_send`, `sessions_spawn`, recovery compaction and two signed-in people through a real Gateway with a scripted model, asserting what the model received, which runs executed, the transcript and pending inputs.

- On this head: 12 of 12 pass, twice.
- On `main` at the merge base (`bd2dbfdeb49`): the recovery-compaction scenario fails exactly as this PR describes. The correction is downgraded to a separate later turn and never reaches the original run. Everything else passes on both, pinning behavior this PR must preserve.

One question for you: in a Control UI conversation, a message sent during a subagent announcement runs as its own turn on `main`, but **joins the announcement run** with this PR. Control UI announcements are `result-required`, so this looks like your "compatible required-to-required steering". Can you confirm it's intended? The test asserts only what must hold either way (answered once, one announcement, nothing pending); `docs/concepts/queue-steering.md` doesn't cover this case yet.

Separately, while building the restart scenarios I found a pre-existing bug that also reproduces on `main`. If a restart interrupts a turn and a new message arrives before restart recovery starts, both inputs stay queued indefinitely. I'm tracking it separately; it isn't caused by this PR.

@jalehman Yes: compatible human input joining a visible Control UI announcement that is already `result-required` is intended. It retains the announcement's execution owner, permissions and required result; it does not cancel the announcement or promote optional work. Optional background work still leaves the human input in followup custody, and `/followup` remains the explicit separate-turn choice. I documented that distinction and extended the existing controller custody table with direct required/result-required acceptance and optional refusal in `c879cc97b939dc4534d33c75b89b5deae36a9975`.

I pulled your two commits unchanged. Your distinction between a retired child and an owed yielded-cohort cancellation report is correct; the body now reflects that retained debt. The independent Muse/UI/xAI/reconnect fixes remain extracted.

The full failing lint logs on this PR and #178985 contain the same four typed errors, beyond the max-lines warnings shown in annotations. The synchronous notice contract left three asynchronous no-op fixtures and one await of void. They reproduce locally before the small test-only repair in c879 and disappear afterward, with assertions unchanged. Validation passes: 132 focused tests, both owning test type graphs, scoped lint/format/docs links and independent review. I also ran all 12 of your public-Gateway scenarios once against the unchanged 6f5 production code; all pass. That uses synthetic state and a scripted HTTP model, not native/live-model inference.

I am keeping #178985 stacked as you requested. Its stack needs the fixture repair before fresh CI; it can retarget after the consolidation lands. GitHub now reports four new test-file conflicts against current upstream, which I am resolving before requesting the next exact-head review/security acknowledgement.

For the separate restart-before-recovery/new-input deadlock, please share the tracking issue or your reproducer branch when available. The existing predecessor-handoff path is already present, so I want to trace your actual blocked dispatch and coordinate one repair owner rather than add another queue policy. It remains explicitly outside the passing twelve scenarios and is not claimed fixed.

@clawsweeper re-review

The branch and PR body are current at `223d8959a0d02c4daab9076c037cfedf282d3a3f`. The reported conflicts are resolved by merging upstream `20d2826d7c6466b000a48a62067b787e69dcd556`; the four manual resolutions are test-only and preserve the cancellation, source-binding, cooperative-wait and peer-scheduling contracts. Jalehman's owed-yielded-wake/best-effort-notice corrections and extracted-PR scope split remain intact.

The previous maintainer answer is now documented and tested: compatible human input can join an already visible `result-required` announcement without changing execution permissions or promoting optional work. Explicit followup remains a separate turn. The four actual typed-lint errors shared with #178985 are repaired without removing assertions or changing production guards.

Validation: 170 affected tests; core, harness/tool, compaction and TUI test type graphs; scoped typed lint/format; and independent P0–P2 review of the manual resolutions all pass. A frozen-lockfile local install corrected an outdated checkout dependency; no package manifest or lockfile change was introduced. Ten focused TUI cases also pass. The canonical isolated QA build passes, and all twelve unchanged #178985 public-RPC Gateway scenarios pass on this production head (54.50s). These use synthetic state and a scripted HTTP model, not live native-Codex or operator data. Earlier traces retain their original revisions and limitations.

#178985 remains separate and stacked as requested. The separately reported restart-before-recovery/new-input deadlock is not claimed fixed by these scenarios; the prior request for its tracking issue/reproducer stands. Exact-head hosted CI and the required maintainer/security approval remain external gates; local verification does not grant that approval.

CI attribution for current head `e3a25eba1ae4737d69b913c8effc7455ee21195d`, [run 39615810386](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39615810386): the four failed test jobs are inherited test-fixture/assertion drift, and their repairs stay outside this consolidation.

| Failed job | Determining failure | Upstream repair |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `checks-node-changed-1` | Three background-exec restart cases exit before readiness on retired `agents.defaults.heartbeat` | #179626; identical subset #179621 is closed as redundant |
| `checks-node-changed-compact-small-38` | Concurrent HTTP streams fixture rejected by the same configuration check | #179626, also covered by narrower #179594; its patch matches the independently derived correction |
| `checks-node-changed-compact-small-8` | First-turn binding fixture rejected by the same configuration check | #179626, also covered by narrower #179592; its patch matches the independently derived correction |
| `checks-ui-e2e (3/9)` | Native titlebar test still requires a shadow after upstream #179214 changed keyboard focus to an outline | Existing #179574; also waits for the upstream hover transition |

The Node fixtures, complete configuration-validator tree and determining startup helpers are identical between this PR and upstream base `53a236d1e49d50661d35f0f51fadadd3a1e63e32`. Local reproduction reached the same configuration failures before lifecycle behavior. The original three restart failures are also recorded in the linked hosted job.

The browser case failed locally at its earlier immediate hover-style read. Reverting this PR's only UI production delta and rebuilding through the canonical browser harness reproduced that exact failure. Upstream #179214 introduced both the transition and outline. With the corresponding test-only repair on upstream production base `53a236d`, all 11 native-nav cases pass. Our independent focus check used the outline offset; #179574 additionally checks visible outline color. This is supporting contract evidence, not a claim to have executed that PR's complete two-file diff.

The earlier ClawSweeper 390px account-menu finding is already repaired upstream by #179307 (`d2590fe9072`). Its exact named case passes on the current integration, with the UI production delta reverted, and on upstream base with the separate test repairs. No additional geometry tolerance change is added here.

On upstream production base with the three independent heartbeat-fixture corrections, all six selected Gateway tests pass: first-turn binding, both concurrent-stream tests, and managed/SIGTERM/SIGKILL restart cases. The restart file takes 77.30s; the canonical runtime build, affected root-other and UI E2E type graphs, scoped restart typed lint/format, and independent P0–P2 review pass. These are synthetic isolated Gateway/browser tests, not new native-Codex or operator-data proof.

No test repair was added to this PR's branch, and no further upstream merge was performed. The branch remains mergeable. The aggregate CI failure and exact-head security approval are not claimed green; maintainer security acceptance and the documented compatible same-requester human/completion-context decision remain open. Existing exact-review artifact failures/retries are owned by ClawSweeper's durable queue.

<details>
<summary>Preserved prior integration evidence (223d checkpoint; not current-head proof)</summary>

## Maintainer follow-up (2026-10-21)

Current head `223d8959a0d02c4daab9076c037cfedf282d3a3f` merges upstream `20d2826d7c6466b000a48a62067b787e69dcd556` after GitHub reported four test-file conflicts. The manual resolutions adopt upstream fixture simplifications while preserving source-cancellation propagation, source-binding result fixtures, both real-Agent cooperative-wait regressions, and precise separate-peer-turn guidance. Incoming production changes are upstream changes; manual conflict repairs are test-only.

Jalehman's `d18b29691a6` owed-yielded-wake/best-effort-notice corrections and `6f5fca7d891` scope split remain intact. Follow-up `c879cc97b939dc4534d33c75b89b5deae36a9975` documents intentional compatible human steering into visible `result-required` announcements while optional work still queues, and extends the existing custody table. It also fixes the four reproducible typed-lint errors shared by this PR and stacked #178985: three asynchronous no-op notice fixtures and one await of void. Assertions and production guards are unchanged; the max-lines diagnostics were warnings.

Validation on the integrated candidate: 170 affected tests across six files, core types, the harness/tool and compaction test type graphs, scoped typed lint/format, and fresh independent P0–P2 manual-resolution review pass. The TUI test type graph also passes after a frozen-lockfile local install restored the already-declared `pi-tui` 1.2.0; no manifest or lockfile changes were made. Ten focused TUI tests also pass after that local install. The earlier c879 follow-up separately passed 132 focused checks and docs checks.

The canonical isolated QA build passes (2m 9.6s). All twelve unchanged synthetic public-RPC Gateway scenarios from stacked #178985 pass on production head `223d8959a0d02c4daab9076c037cfedf282d3a3f` (54.50s), including compatible announcement steering and compaction recovery. They use a scripted HTTP model and synthetic state; this is not live native-Codex or operator-data proof. The earlier twelve-scenario run passed before upstream integration as well. The author's reported upstream-negative compaction result remains author-reported evidence for its stated revision.

#178985 stays separate and stacked as its author requests; refresh its stack for the fixture repairs, then retarget after this PR lands. Exact-head hosted CI and fresh maintainer security approval remain required. The separately reported restart-before-recovery/new-input deadlock is not claimed fixed or covered by these twelve scenarios. No operator Gateway was deployed or restarted for this work.


</details>

<!-- openclaw-merge:ac05203e-57ac-46e4-8311-36aa7cb8a7f8 -->

Two independent follow-up bugs now have narrow fixes on top of this merged consolidation:

- #180704: an obsolete restored child-completion reservation could park new chat input before an execution starts.
- #180728: a child correctly retained its own admitted execution authority, but the in-process facade still checked its recovered parent’s retired work claim afterward. This complements the merged child-authority repairs #176769, #178186, and #178693.

The PRs cross-link and include synthetic regression and isolated built-Gateway restart evidence. They do not depend on one another or introduce the separated messaging, requester-selection, or reply-obligation policies.
